question: Should this zero-diff draft rollback artifact be retained temporarily for incident response, or closed now that the forward fix is merged on `main`?
rationale: The branch is intentionally non-production material, and deciding whether rollback preparedness outweighs retaining a confusing no-op draft is an operational ownership choice rather than a mechanical code repair.

options.title: Close the no-op draft
options.body: Close it as non-mergeable rollback material and require any future rollback to be rebuilt against the then-current `main` after a production diagnosis.

options.title: Retain as temporary incident material
options.body: Keep it draft-only with a clear owner and expiry, while prohibiting merge until a fresh diagnosis and runtime proof are attached.

recommendation.title: Close the no-op draft
recommendation.body: Close it as non-mergeable rollback material and require any future rollback to be rebuilt against the then-current `main` after a production diagnosis.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the merged forward fix and this explicit rollback artifact, making them the closest available technical context holder.
